declared_purpose: Provide OpenClaw agents with programmatic Claude Code command execution, file operations, searches, persistent sessions, agent teams and tool controls (SKILL.md:2-3,24-26,46-57). The entry explicitly recommends persistent sessions for multi-step tasks (SKILL.md:317-326). Supporting modules implement MCP client management and optional chat persistence. Broad environment inheritance, credential storage and diagnostic dumps are implementation choices, rather than explicit requirements.

data_operations.operation: Read local routing and directory metadata
data_operations.source: CLI process environment and current working directory
data_operations.data_scope: SASHA_DOCTOR_URL selects the backend; continue defaults its working-directory argument to process.cwd().
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI memory; selected URL controls HTTP requests, and the directory is included in /continue requests.
data_operations.condition: CLI execution; directory discovery applies to continue without --cwd. The backend defaults to loopback, so network requests are not necessarily remote disclosures.

data_operations.operation: Dispatch requested commands, file operations and searches
data_operations.data_scope: Commands and descriptions; file paths; tool names and arbitrary JSON arguments, potentially including write content; search patterns, directories and output controls; batch-read patterns and base directory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured backend under /sasha-doctor/claude-code at /bash, /read, /call and /batch-read. Returned content goes to caller-facing stdout or stderr.
data_operations.condition: Only the selected command runs. The CLI sends selectors and arguments; backend file reads, writes and command execution are not implemented in the supplied source. Ordinary results need not leave the caller.

data_operations.operation: Transmit session configuration and access controls
data_operations.source: session-start arguments and generated session name
data_operations.data_scope: Name, working directory, resume/custom session identifiers, model, baseUrl, permission mode, tool controls, budgets, prompts, agent definitions and additional directories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured backend /sasha-doctor/claude-code/session/start; selected identifiers and options are printed locally.
data_operations.condition: session-start invocation. Most fields are optional; permission mode defaults to acceptEdits. Sending baseUrl configures the backend and does not itself demonstrate a request to that model endpoint.

data_operations.operation: Transmit task text and receive responses
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied prompts, messages and session selectors
data_operations.data_scope: Prompt/message text, session name or identifier, optional working directory and send timeout.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured backend /resume, /continue, /session/send or /session/send-stream; responses, streaming text, tool names and errors return to caller-facing stdout/stderr.
data_operations.condition: Requested resume, continue or session-send operation. Streaming prints text and tool names, but only a completion indicator for tool-result events.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve session metadata, usage statistics and history
data_operations.source: Backend responses to sessions, session-list, session-status, session-history and session-search
data_operations.data_scope: Session identifiers, names, paths, summaries, timestamps, message counts, readiness, token/tool/turn counts and conversation events. Search requests disclose query, project, time filter and limit.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI memory and caller-facing output. History text is shortened for display after retrieval. Statistics and summaries are supplied by the backend; their derivation is not shown.
data_operations.condition: Explicit listing, status, history or search invocation. sessions applies its display limit locally; history and search transmit limits.

data_operations.source: Caller-supplied session names and fork name
data_operations.data_scope: Names identifying sessions to stop, pause, resume, fork or restart.
data_operations.condition: Explicit lifecycle command. Pause is described as saving state and fork as branching, but backend persistence/copying is unresolved. Stop is not evidence of deletion.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist MCP server configuration
data_operations.source: Configuration file and caller-supplied ServerConfig objects
data_operations.data_scope: Server identifiers, executable commands, arguments, status and configured environment values. Example credential variables include GITHUB_TOKEN and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CONFIG_PATH, defaulting to process.cwd()/mcp_config.json; writes serialize the complete configuration as JSON. Several management actions return the configuration to their caller.
data_operations.condition: Auxiliary MCP module invocation. Adding and changing server status writes configuration; reads fall back to an empty default on failure. Credential values are persisted if included in config.env.

data_operations.operation: Pass host environment and server-specific configuration to an MCP transport
data_operations.data_scope: Every defined host environment variable, overlaid with config.env, plus configured command and arguments.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: StdioClientTransport configured for the selected MCP subprocess; this is a local process boundary, not demonstrated remote transmission.
data_operations.condition: createClient invocation. Automatic initialization skips paused servers; explicit resume creates a client. The example GitHub server is active and Slack server paused.

data_operations.operation: Discover, cache and expose MCP tool metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Tool discovery responses, client identifiers, connection state and initialization error messages.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-memory clientsMap, management callers and stdout. Initialization logs the complete tool discovery response through the logger.
data_operations.condition: Auxiliary MCP initialization or status/tool retrieval. Tool discovery is needed for tool availability; the full diagnostic dump is an additional output.

data_operations.operation: Forward an MCP request and return its result
data_operations.data_scope: The complete request, including method and arbitrary parameters; returned result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected connected MCP client/server via client.request; result returns directly to the invoking caller. The wrapper logs the client identifier and errors.
data_operations.condition: executeMcpAction with an available client. Actual server file access, external requests and retention are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Close MCP clients and remove local configuration or runtime records
data_operations.data_scope: Selected server configuration and in-memory connection/tool/error records.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local configuration file and process memory; client.close is requested.
data_operations.condition: Pause preserves configuration with paused status and drops the runtime entry; remove deletes the configuration entry and runtime entry; restart closes clients and clears the map. These actions do not demonstrate deletion of data held by servers.

data_operations.source: Basic MCP example and selected filesystem server
data_operations.data_scope: Current-directory access configuration, server status, tool metadata and directory listing result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured local filesystem MCP server and example stdout; addMcpServer also persists its configuration.
data_operations.condition: If the example is made runnable and invoked. It configures './' and calls list_directory for './'; file-content reading is not demonstrated by this example.

data_operations.operation: Persist and hydrate optional application state
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied state, persistence options and storage adapter
data_operations.data_scope: Serializable application state, hydration flag and update timestamp, subject to caller persistence options.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured persistence storage. The supplied adapter reads idb-keyval storage first and falls back to window.localStorage; writes prefer IndexedDB and fall back on exceptions.
data_operations.condition: Auxiliary store factory invocation. Normal adapter writes skip state without _hasHydrated; exceptions enter the localStorage fallback. No expiry is implemented in these files.

data_operations.operation: Create and persist chat content and temporal metadata
data_operations.source: Chat example method inputs and generated identifiers/timestamps
data_operations.data_scope: Session topics, roles, message content, session/message identifiers, message dates, session update times and current-session identifier.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Example store memory and the persistence adapter under key chat-store. Example output includes the complete current sessions array.
data_operations.condition: If the chat example is made runnable. Its main function adds fixture content; the methods also accept caller-supplied chat data and hydration can recover earlier sessions. Generated metadata is not evidence of personal-attribute inference.

data_operations.operation: Merge supplied state locally and logically delete chat sessions
data_operations.source: Caller-provided local/remote objects and session arrays
data_operations.data_scope: State fields and chat sessions/messages. Sessions merge by identifier, missing messages are appended and dates determine ordering. deleteSession filters the current session array.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller memory; the chat example sets merged or filtered sessions into its persistent store. No network synchronization is implemented.
data_operations.condition: Explicit utility/method invocation. A previously deleted session can be re-added if a later supplied remote array contains its nonempty history; there is no deletion tombstone.

data_operations.operation: Delete storage entries or clear a storage namespace
data_operations.source: Storage adapter removeItem and clear calls
data_operations.data_scope: Named persisted value for removeItem; the entire idb-keyval store for clear, or the entire localStorage namespace on fallback.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: IndexedDB first; localStorage only if the IndexedDB deletion/clear throws.
data_operations.condition: Explicit adapter deletion calls. Successful IndexedDB deletion does not also delete an existing localStorage copy. Secure erasure and deletion of external copies are not established.

data_operations.source: String passed to MCP utility functions
data_operations.data_scope: Tagged client identifier and embedded JSON request.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling process and returned object only.
data_operations.condition: Explicit utility invocation. Extraction does not itself execute the request, transmit it or persist the content.

potential_excess.data_scope: All defined host environment variables, including unrelated credentials or personal configuration if present.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Each configured MCP subprocess through StdioClientTransport.env.
potential_excess.condition: Auxiliary createClient execution; automatic initialization excludes paused servers.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: MCP servers need an executable environment and their own configuration. Forwarding unrelated host variables adds data to a necessary process-start action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Start the selected server with required runtime variables and its authorized credentials.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a minimal runtime environment plus an explicit per-server allowlist and required config.env values.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain variables required for executable discovery, platform operation and the selected server's authentication.

potential_excess.data_scope: Credential values supplied in config.env, such as GITHUB_TOKEN or SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Plain JSON at CONFIG_PATH, default process.cwd()/mcp_config.json.
potential_excess.condition: Configuration updates involving servers whose env contains credentials; paused configurations are also retained.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Server configuration persistence supports management and restart, but credential bytes need not share the ordinary configuration-file boundary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve server settings and make required credentials available when the server starts.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Persist credential references or variable names and resolve values from a runtime credential provider.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Ensure startup, resume and restart can resolve the correct server-specific credentials without broad environment inheritance.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete MCP tool discovery responses, including descriptions, schemas and any additional returned metadata.
potential_excess.condition: Successful initializeSingleClient tool discovery; this info log is not gated by debugMode.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Discovery and caching support tool use. Serializing the complete response to stdout is a redundant diagnostic action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Cache tool definitions and make them available to explicit tool-list callers.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log only initialization success and a tool count by default; make detailed metadata an explicit diagnostic option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the complete in-memory discovery result available for actual tool selection and invocation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Tool definitions beyond the availability/count information displayed by status.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Backend-to-CLI response and CLI memory at /tools.
potential_excess.condition: status invokes the same /tools retrieval used for listing, then displays only connection state and tools.length.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Checking connection status requires a response and count, rather than complete tool definitions; this is extra response data in a required check.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report connection availability and tool count.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Provide a status/count endpoint or server-side response projection.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the existing connection test and count semantics; backend support must be implemented or confirmed.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session entries beyond the caller's requested sessions --limit.
potential_excess.condition: The backend returns more entries than the display limit; the request sends no limit and slicing happens after retrieval.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Displaying recent sessions is required. Receiving undisplayed entries adds data to that required retrieval.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Display the requested number of recent sessions with their selected metadata.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Transmit the limit and enforce it at the backend before returning session records.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve ordering and requested fields; backend limit support is unresolved.

potential_excess.data_scope: History text beyond displayed previews and event fields unused by the CLI renderer.
potential_excess.condition: Returned history includes long text or other event fields; text is shortened to 60 characters only after retrieval.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The command displays event previews. Excess text is extra data within the required history request, rather than a separate redundant request.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Show the requested event count, time, type and current text/tool preview.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request a backend preview projection containing display fields and a truncation indicator; reserve full events for an explicit full-history option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve preview selection, ordering, count and ellipsis behavior; backend projection support is unresolved.

potential_excess.data_scope: Previously persisted application/chat state remaining in localStorage after successful IndexedDB deletion or replacement.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: window.localStorage[name], separate from the IndexedDB primary copy.
potential_excess.condition: A prior fallback created a localStorage value, then primary storage succeeds. removeItem and clear touch fallback storage only on primary failure; reads can later recover the stale fallback.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Fallback storage supports recovery, but retaining obsolete or deleted copies exceeds the current-state persistence purpose.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Maintain usable fallback persistence and honor deletion of the selected persisted state.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove stale fallback keys after successful primary writes and attempt deletion in both backends, reporting partial failure.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain fallback writes when primary storage fails and preserve unrelated storage keys.

potential_excess.data_scope: All current chat sessions, including previously hydrated topics, messages and metadata.
potential_excess.condition: The optional example runs with existing sessions; its final console.log prints the entire sessions array.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Demonstrating persistence and recovery does not require dumping existing conversations. This is a redundant disclosure to an output channel.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Demonstrate hydration, creation and addition of the example message.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Print session counts and the newly created session identifier instead of complete sessions.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep persistence and recovery behavior intact; retain explicit content inspection only when requested.

unknowns: All supplied files were reviewed. The backend implementation is absent, so actual backend file access, command execution, permission enforcement, session retention, fork copying and deletion remain unresolved. CLI lifecycle requests do not establish those outcomes (src/index.ts:513-644,708-719; SKILL.md:362-374).

Downstream model/proxy payloads, recipients, authentication and retention are unknown. The CLI forwards baseUrl to the backend; it does not implement the onward model request (src/index.ts:332-385; SKILL.md:289-305).

Auxiliary MCP/store behavior is conditional, not demonstrated on the packaged CLI path. package.json points to dist/index.js, while src/index.ts imports only commander and exports none of the names imported by the examples. SDK, zod, zustand and idb-keyval dependencies are also absent from the manifest; runtime availability was not tested (package.json:6-13,21-29; src/index.ts:7-10,721-721; examples/basic-mcp.ts:8-15; examples/chat-store.ts:8-13).

MCP SDK, configured server packages and storage dependencies are outside the supplied source. Their subprocess behavior, external disclosures, persistence, and IndexedDB database/store namespace cannot be established (src/mcp/client.ts:5-9,19-41; src/store/indexeddb-storage.ts:5-6).

No packaged source establishes capture, forwarding or retention of stdout/stderr. Output findings identify that boundary without assuming a log service or additional recipient (src/mcp/logger.ts:55-58; examples/chat-store.ts:152-152).
Backend support for status projections, session limits and history previews is unknown; proposed response reductions require corresponding backend behavior (src/index.ts:200-224,561-570).
The documented CLAUDE_CODE_API_URL alias is not read by the supplied CLI, which selects its backend using SASHA_DOCTOR_URL only (README.md:78-87; src/index.ts:9-10).
